title: How To Do Pirouettes, Fouettés, and À La Seconde Turns! I Dance Turn Tutorial with @trainwithkendall

method.teacher_system: The teacher breaks down dance turns into clear, sequential pieces: parallel pirouettes, ballet pirouettes, à la seconde turns, and fouettés. She teaches foundational positions and alignments like rib cage closure before adding rotation.
method.signature: Her playful, highly encouraging tone combined with self-deprecating humor ("try this a couple million times") makes intimidating ballet turns feel achievable.

practices.what: Breaks down the tutorial into three main sections: pirouettes, fouettés, and à la seconde turns.
Focuses on upper body alignment by lifting the chin, pressing shoulders down, and closing the rib cage before turning.
Practices the plié and passé position connection multiple times before attempting to add rotation.
Teaches ballet pirouettes by adapting the parallel pirouette mechanics into first position with outward rotators.
Instructs learners to practice the plié-passé combination multiple times to build muscle memory.
Breaks down the à la seconde turn into progressive steps: slap prep, corner hold, and then rotation.
Suggests doing 10 repetitions of just the slap prep and corner position before turning.
Outlines a structured practice routine: slap prep, corner hold, second hold, and finally piecing them together.
Suggests using a chair, bar, or stable household object as a support when practicing fouettés at home.
Breaks down fouetté preparation at the barre using three distinct leg positions: front, side, and passé.

adaptations.difficulty: Needing support for fouetté turns at home without a ballet barre
adaptations.adjustment: Grab a chair or something stable in your house to hold onto

beliefs.belief: Turns should be compact and executed as a single, cohesive movement rather than disconnected sections.

feelings.response: Acknowledge that à la seconde turns are complicated, but encourage learners not to give up on them.

struggles.theme: À la seconde turns were very difficult and exhausting
Not enough space in the room to practice leg extensions
Struggling to hold leg high enough during turns

clicked.theme: Explanation of closing the rib cage made turns finally click
Step-by-step instructions are easy to understand and apply

requests.theme: Ask the teacher to hold a dance academy or be their ongoing teacher

meant.theme: Helped adult beginners and self-taught dancers learn proper technique at home

method.limits: The video is recorded in a plain studio setting with only one instructor, so partner-work and full-group spatial dynamics cannot be shown.
